decisions.title: Local capability protocol identity
decisions.issue: No referenced standard defines a generic capability token, its authority fields, canonical bytes, signed-URL profile, or lifecycle.
interpretations: Define one narrow, explicitly local and versioned capability protocol
decisions.peer_behavior: JWT, PASETO, Macaroons, OAuth access tokens, and provider signed URLs encode different trust, delegation, caveat, and canonicalization models.
decisions.selected_behavior: cap1 is a local v1 protocol for explicitly encoded resource operations.
decisions.rationale: A distinct identity prevents importing incompatible token semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: The narrow profile prevents accidental authority widening.
decisions.resource_consequences: Every field and token length remains bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Another token family requires a separate adapter.
decisions.wire_consequences: Consumers must treat the complete cap1 grammar as the wire contract.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream specification owns this local profile.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately versioned profile is designed against a named external protocol with complete independent interoperability evidence.

decisions.title: Algorithm and key-type binding
decisions.issue: Standards define algorithms but do not authorize a token header to choose trusted verification policy, bind one key ID to several key types, or downgrade after a mismatch.
interpretations: Require an exact trusted algorithm and key-type binding
decisions.peer_behavior: Python 3's maintained standard-library HMAC implementation agrees with the package's HMAC-SHA-256 bytes for the pinned capability fixture.
decisions.selected_behavior: The package supports only HMAC-SHA-256 and Ed25519.
decisions.rationale: Exact trusted key binding prevents algorithm confusion and downgrade.
decisions.security_consequences: Algorithm confusion and downgrade are rejected before expensive or alternate verification.
decisions.resource_consequences: HMAC keys are copied and bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Adding another algorithm requires an additive protocol decision and new independent vectors.
decisions.wire_consequences: The algorithm names hmac-sha256 and ed25519 are local profile values.
decisions.upstream_status: No package-specific erratum changes the pinned algorithm bytes.
decisions.reconsider_when: A concrete cryptographic migration has reviewed standard-library support, downgrade analysis, vectors, and a versioning plan.

decisions.title: Canonical JSON and token framing
decisions.issue: JSON object ordering, duplicate member handling, optional-field omission, numeric spelling, Unicode normalization, and base64url padding are not one universal signed representation.
interpretations: Define one encoder and require byte-for-byte canonical re-encoding
decisions.peer_behavior: Python 3's maintained standard-library base64 and HMAC implementations reproduce the exact pinned canonical token.
decisions.selected_behavior: Tokens contain exactly three unpadded base64url segments after the cap1 prefix.
decisions.rationale: One byte representation prevents parser and signature differentials.
decisions.security_consequences: One signed byte representation prevents duplicate-member, normalization, and alternate-encoding ambiguity.
decisions.resource_consequences: Token, segment, member, collection, and decoded-byte limits apply before authority is returned.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Producers must emit the package canonical form.
decisions.wire_consequences: Semantically similar but differently ordered, padded, duplicated, normalized, or numerically spelled inputs are rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 8259 does not define this signature canonicalization.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new token version adopts a published canonical JSON profile and migration preserves old verification until expiry.

decisions.title: Time interval and skew semantics
decisions.issue: Issued-at, not-before, expiration, integer precision, equality boundaries, skew direction, and maximum lifetime can be interpreted differently even when all parties use Unix seconds.
interpretations: One explicit half-open validity interval with bounded skew
decisions.peer_behavior: Token libraries vary on inclusive expiration and whether skew extends not-before, expiry, or both.
decisions.selected_behavior: Canonical values are UTC Unix seconds.
decisions.rationale: A half-open interval gives every equality boundary one stable meaning.
decisions.security_consequences: Finite lifetime and skew bound stolen-token exposure.
decisions.resource_consequences: Caller-provided current time is explicit and no hidden clock or timer exists.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Subsecond values are intentionally truncated at issuance into canonical seconds.
decisions.wire_consequences: A token is invalid exactly at expiration plus accepted skew.
decisions.upstream_status: No referenced standard defines the complete interval.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new profile needs different precision or interval semantics and can be versioned without reinterpreting issued tokens.

decisions.title: Encoded authority and application authorization
decisions.issue: Signature verification proves token integrity but does not prove that a concrete caller may perform an attempted operation.
interpretations: Require an explicit attempted-use comparison after verification
decisions.peer_behavior: General claim-token middleware often places decoded claims in context and leaves enforcement implicit.
decisions.selected_behavior: Verify authenticates encoded authority and Grant.Authorize separately compares every attempted dimension.
decisions.rationale: Verification and authorization are separate security decisions.
decisions.security_consequences: Callers cannot accidentally treat a valid signature as universal access through the typed API.
decisions.resource_consequences: Caveat size and count are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications changing resource vocabulary or caveat semantics must version their profile.
decisions.wire_consequences: Missing, extra, or mismatched authority dimensions reject use.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 supplies the adjacent distinction while the capability dimensions remain package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately specified attenuation or delegated-caveat model defines complete evaluation and compatibility semantics.

decisions.title: Signed URL canonicalization
decisions.issue: Raw and parsed URLs can disagree around userinfo, default ports, case, escaped paths, dot segments, encoded slashes, duplicate query values, fragments, relative references, and parameter ordering.
interpretations: Define one strict profile and reject every non-canonical alternative
decisions.peer_behavior: Provider signed URLs use incompatible covered components and normalization.
decisions.selected_behavior: A named immutable profile allowlists schemes, canonical authorities, query names, and one signature parameter.
decisions.rationale: Signing and routing must use one interpretation.
decisions.security_consequences: Rejecting alternate routing representations prevents authority substitution and parameter smuggling.
decisions.resource_consequences: URL, path, query, parameter, and value sizes are finite before signing or verification.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Canonicalization changes require a new profile name or token version.
decisions.wire_consequences: Ambiguous but otherwise parseable URLs are incompatible.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 3986 does not define this signing profile.
decisions.reconsider_when: A named external signed-URL profile is implemented in an isolated adapter with differential vectors.

decisions.title: Covered HTTP method, origin, and body digest
decisions.issue: A URL alone does not bind request method, externally trusted origin, proxy rewriting, or body bytes.
interpretations: Require an explicit profile, trusted origin, exact method, and digest pairing
decisions.peer_behavior: Reverse proxies and signed-URL providers disagree on forwarded-origin trust and covered request components.
decisions.selected_behavior: The profile signs the exact configured method and canonical URL.
decisions.rationale: Every authority-bearing transport dimension must be explicitly trusted or signed.
decisions.security_consequences: Proxy-controlled fields cannot redirect authority, downgrade scheme, or omit body integrity.
decisions.resource_consequences: The package does not buffer arbitrary bodies.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Rewriting any covered component invalidates verification.
decisions.wire_consequences: Method case, origin, path, query, profile, expiration, and optional digest are signed dimensions.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 does not define this capability signature profile or proxy trust model.
decisions.reconsider_when: A deployment adopts a separately specified proxy-origin contract or streaming digest profile with equivalent ambiguity analysis.

decisions.title: Bounded-use replay consumption
decisions.issue: One-time and bounded-use capabilities require a single atomic owner.
interpretations: Expose atomic store ownership and unknown outcomes explicitly
decisions.peer_behavior: Token middleware commonly treats replay as cache membership.
decisions.selected_behavior: Positive MaxUses values require an explicit ConsumptionStore that atomically binds capability identity, expiry, and maximum uses.
decisions.rationale: One atomic state owner is required to prevent concurrent overuse.
decisions.security_consequences: Atomic consumption prevents concurrent overuse when the selected store is shared by all replicas.
decisions.resource_consequences: Counts, identities, expiry, and cleanup are bounded.
decisions.wire_consequences: Use count is signed and cannot be changed by storage policy.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 idempotency does not resolve capability transaction commit ambiguity.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new adapter proves equivalent atomicity, durability, expiry, and unknown-outcome semantics under its deployment topology.

decisions.title: Revocation matching and consistency
decisions.issue: Revocation by capability, key, subject, resource, tenant, or issue time has different scope.
interpretations: Expose exact match dimensions and let adapters document consistency
decisions.peer_behavior: Token systems use deny lists, key removal, short expiry, epochs, or provider introspection with different propagation guarantees.
decisions.selected_behavior: Verification submits an exact bounded RevocationQuery and outage or cancellation fails closed.
decisions.rationale: Exact dimensions avoid wildcard broadening and explicit outages avoid silent acceptance.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact dimensions prevent accidental wildcard broadening.
decisions.resource_consequences: Queries and retained process-local entries are bounded by application policy.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Deployments must account for the configured store's propagation window.
decisions.wire_consequences: Revocation does not alter token bytes.
decisions.upstream_status: There is no upstream capability-v1 revocation standard.
decisions.reconsider_when: A durable revocation adapter defines measurable propagation, outage, and recovery semantics that require additive public policy.

decisions.title: Key resolution and lifecycle snapshots
decisions.issue: Key rotation, overlap, disablement, revocation, unknown IDs, remote latency, stale caches, and provider diagnostics can change acceptance or leak sensitive material.
interpretations: Retry or fetch without a bound
Use immutable local snapshots and one bounded caller-owned resolution operation
decisions.peer_behavior: JOSE key resolvers often refresh remote sets automatically and token libraries may collapse unknown key and algorithm mismatch.
decisions.selected_behavior: KeySet is an immutable exact key-ID snapshot and BoundedResolver performs one bounded caller-owned resolution operation.
decisions.rationale: Explicit snapshots and bounded lookup keep lifecycle and remote ownership observable.
decisions.security_consequences: Provider secrets and causes are discarded from public errors.
decisions.resource_consequences: Lookup count, key-ID length, algorithms, and duration are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Distributed propagation depends on caller-owned resolver deployment.
decisions.wire_consequences: A key is accepted only while its exact trusted lifecycle permits it.
decisions.upstream_status: Cryptographic source standards do not define application resolver lifecycle.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separate cache or remote-key adapter specifies freshness, synchronization, shutdown, outage, and compromise behavior without changing the core contract.

decisions.title: HTTP middleware failure and ownership boundary
decisions.issue: Middleware can conflate verification with authorization or consumption, expose token/provider details, read bodies implicitly, commit partial responses, or permit a failed request to reach the application.
interpretations: Verify only and return one bounded secret-safe adapter response
decisions.peer_behavior: Framework token middleware often combines parsing, authentication, claims context, and policy.
decisions.selected_behavior: caphttp.Verifier verifies before calling the next handler and leaves authorization, consumption, and protected side effects explicit.
decisions.rationale: The adapter must not hide application-owned security and side-effect ordering.
decisions.security_consequences: Invalid capability bytes, keys, signatures, caveats, and provider causes are not reflected.
decisions.resource_consequences: Middleware performs no hidden body buffering, service lookup, goroutine, retry, or state mutation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications needing another representation configure an explicit handler without changing verification semantics.
decisions.wire_consequences: The default failure status and body are package policy, not a standardized capability response.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 defines general response semantics but no capability-v1 transport mapping.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately versioned public API profile standardizes capability failures, authorization, or consumption ordering.
